$comment: Canonical answer_category decisions. Read by the feasibility skill when a label is arguable, and by skills/shared/tests/run_tests.py, which asserts this table is internally consistent and that every rule it cites exists. One file rather than a table in each of the rubric and the specification, because the production defect this exists to fix WAS a drift defect: nothing stated the tie-break, so the agent invented one per call and contradicted itself between calls. `doc_phrase` is the phrase each rule is stated under in the prose surfaces; the test asserts the prose states all eight in this order, so a reordering edit to either document fails here rather than silently giving the reviewer two different rankings.

procedure.test: The answer is a person's name, a date, a clock time, a span of time, a currency amount, or a count/measure.
procedure.note: Decided by what the answer IS, before any judgement about the setting. date/time/duration never merge; price is currency only, so '10 lessons' is quantity.

procedure.test: The answer is the name of employment, a vacancy, or a role a person performs.
procedure.note: A job title describes what a person is engaged as. It is not the facility where the person works or the service they perform.

procedure.doc_phrase: artefact beats the thing it governs
procedure.test: The answer names an official artefact or record identifier that is issued, carried, shown, signed, quoted or presented.
procedure.note: Ranked above facility and service on purpose. A 'parking permit' is a document even though parking is a facility and issuing it is a service: the answer is the artefact, and the rule is to judge the answer rather than what surrounds it.

procedure.doc_phrase: is a route to a person
procedure.test: The answer is a token used to REACH a person or organisation: a phone number, an extension, an email address.
procedure.note: A reference, booking or property code is NOT contact. It identifies a record, and nobody is reached by quoting it. Such a code is a document under the rule above.

procedure.test: The answer says WHERE something is: an address, a postcode, a place name used as a position.
procedure.note: Ranked above facility: a named place given as an answer to 'where' is a location, and the same name given as an answer to 'what is there' is a facility. The item decides which was asked.

procedure.test: Would the answer still exist with nobody performing it? Yes -> facility. No, it needs someone to do something -> service.
procedure.note: This is the tie-break whose absence produced two directly opposed production rejections in one run: 'breakfast is an included service, not a physical facility' and 'Riverside Brasserie is a physical restaurant venue, so it is a facility rather than a purchasable service'. Both conclusions are correct under this rule, and neither is reachable from 'purchasable versus described' alone -- included breakfast is not purchased, and a named venue is not described. Charged-or-included is NOT the axis; performed-or-present is.

procedure.test: Did the dialogue name two or more alternatives and settle on this one? Only then is it preference. A condition the caller asks for, or must satisfy, is requirement.
procedure.note: The alternatives must be NAMED IN THE SCRIPT. Without them there is no weighing and so no preference -- 'furnished' states a property's existing attribute, and labelling it preference was the third distinct production rejection of this class.

procedure.test: The answer fits none of the 14.
procedure.note: Not a categorisation problem: a material problem. Report it in reasons rather than forcing the closest label.

cases.context: An employment agency names the vacancy being advertised.
cases.why: It names the role the applicant would perform, not the workplace or a service supplied there.

cases.context: A hotel receptionist lists what the nightly rate includes.
cases.why: Someone has to serve it. Included rather than charged, which is why the purchasable/described wording could not settle it.

cases.context: The name of the hotel restaurant where breakfast is served.
cases.why: The venue exists whether or not anyone is working in it. A named place is not made a service by the service happening inside it.

cases.context: The letting agent reads back the property reference for the caller to quote later.
cases.why: Rule 4 excludes contact -- quoting a code reaches no person -- and rule 3 is what assigns the label: a record identifier is quoted the way an artefact is presented. The two rules do different jobs, and only the one that assigns is cited here.

cases.context: The agent states the flat's condition. No unfurnished option is offered.
cases.why: Nothing was weighed against anything. An attribute the caller asks about or accepts is a requirement.

cases.context: The tenant must display one; the agent explains how it is issued.
cases.why: The answer is the permit, not the parking. Displaying it is the point.

cases.context: Asked how far the flat is from transport; the agent names the nearest station.
cases.why: The item asks where, so the named place is a position. Had the item asked what is nearby, the same name would be a facility -- never a preference, since nothing was weighed.
A specification, and form_first settles it before the surrounding sentence gets a vote. The specification's own worked example.

cases.context: The receptionist gives the direct extension for the bookings desk.
cases.why: It reaches a person. The specification's own contact-versus-location pair.

cases.context: The caller reads out the postcode of the property.
cases.why: Where a thing is, not how to reach a person. The other half of the same specification pair.

cases.context: The caller asks for a room the visiting family can use.
cases.why: Asked for rather than already present. The specification's own requirement-versus-facility pair.

cases.context: The agent mentions a park already next to the flat.
cases.why: It exists in the setting and nobody performs it. The other half of the same specification pair.

cases.context: The course fee covers a block of lessons.
cases.why: price is currency only. The specification's own price boundary.
